subject: Architecture
title: Cabrini-Green: Towers of Isolation
description: Learn Cabrini-Green: Towers of Isolation in one minute.

hook.text: Chicago's Cabrini-Green was meant to save the poor from slums. Instead, it became more dangerous than the slums.

buildup.text: Fifteen high-rise towers packed 15,000 residents into isolated blocks — cut off from jobs, shops, and transit.

discovery.text: Long corridors, hidden stairwells, and broken elevators created spaces that residents couldn't safely navigate.

twist.text: The architectural design itself enabled crime — blind corners and empty lobbies offered hiding spots on every floor.

climax.text: Demolition began in 1995. Mixed-income townhouses replaced the towers — smaller, safer, connected to the city.

punchline.text: Towers meant to help people trapped them instead.

quiz.question: What replaced Chicago's Cabrini-Green towers?
options: Commercial office buildings and retail shops
Mixed-income townhouses connected to the city
A public park and community recreation center
